clue.text: Awfully unromantic garment for 2

indicators.note: something done awfully is done badly, so the next word's letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A complaint that some item of clothing is dreadfully unsexy.
explanation.walkthrough: 2 points to the answer of 2-down, the Roman dictator, whose clothing this is.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar and his fellow citizens wore a tunic beneath the toga, the basic dress of ancient Rome.

clue.text: Wacky Races without a leader

indicators.note: read as 'with' plus 'out', meaning the single letter comes along beside the word before it
wacky means crazy, so the letters are thrown into a crazy new order

explanation.surface: The old cartoon Wacky Races, imagined with no one out in front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without a leader' looks like an instruction to drop a first letter; in fact 'leader' is the definition and 'a' is extra fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Julius Caesar was the Roman general and dictator, and his name became a title for emperors and rulers.

clue.text: Conqueror of the Romans

indicators.note: of here means taken from within, so the letters come out of the following words

blocks.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: A general who defeated the might of Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks for a Hannibal or a Goth; the answer is just tucked inside the last two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A hero is a champion, someone who wins glory by victory, as a conqueror does.

clue.text: Mogul has important Turner

blocks.note: a wheel is something that turns

explanation.surface: A tycoon owns a significant painting by the artist J M W Turner.
explanation.walkthrough: Turner looks like the painter, but here it is simply a thing that turns.
explanation.definitionFit: Both terms are informal names for a powerful, influential person in business or organisations.

clue.text: Feel Antony's intrinsic style

indicators.note: intrinsic means lying within, so the letters sit inside the run of words

blocks.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: An invitation to sense Mark Antony's natural flair.
explanation.definitionFit: Elan is flair or dash, a stylish vigour in how something is done.

clue.text: Hymn Horace composed about Ligarius originally

indicators.note: composed means put together, so the poet's name is rearranged
about means around, so the rearranged letters surround the one letter
originally points to the first letter of the name it follows

blocks.note: the Roman poet, taken as written
first letter of the conspirator's name

explanation.surface: The poet Horace writes verse concerning Ligarius, one of Caesar's assassins.
explanation.walkthrough: Ligarius is a conspirator in Shakespeare's Julius Caesar.
explanation.definitionFit: A chorale is a stately hymn tune, typically of the Lutheran church, sung by a choir or congregation.

clue.text: Dictator's criminal conspirator

indicators.note: a dictator is also one who dictates, speaking words aloud for another to write, so the next word is as heard

explanation.surface: A tyrant's crooked accomplice in a plot.
explanation.walkthrough: Dictator looks like Caesar, but means someone speaking. Cinna is one of the plotters against Caesar in Shakespeare's play.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinna joined Brutus and Cassius in the plot that killed Caesar, so he is a named plotter.

clue.text: Relaxes with Latin during day in Rome

indicators.note: during means within the period of, so the letter goes inside the day

blocks.note: the ides was the mid-month day of the Roman calendar

explanation.surface: Someone unwinds with a Latin text on a day spent in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ides of March was the day Caesar was killed.
explanation.definitionFit: To idle is to laze about doing nothing, which is taking it easy.

clue.text: Dog that is following explorer

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the short phrase is placed after the name

blocks.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A hound accompanying a polar expedition leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottie is the familiar name for the Scottish terrier, a small wiry-haired breed.

clue.text: Fresh naan bread in Old Delhi

indicators.note: fresh means new, so the next word is made into something new

explanation.surface: Newly baked Indian flatbread on sale in the old part of Delhi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bread' is slang for money, not the naan.
explanation.definitionFit: The anna was a former Indian coin worth one sixteenth of a rupee, cash in the old currency.

clue.text: Give up opportunity for public display

blocks.note: to shop someone is to inform on them to the police

explanation.surface: Someone forgoes a chance to show themselves in public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give up' is not surrender but betray, the British slang sense of shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop's front glass is where goods are shown to passers-by, and figuratively any showcase.

clue.text: Conversion of dream try finished like Socrates

indicators.note: a conversion changes form, so the following letters are turned into another word

explanation.surface: A rugby conversion of a dream try, said in the same breath as a Greek philosopher.
explanation.walkthrough: Conversion and try look like rugby scoring. Socrates died by drinking hemlock rather than renounce his teaching.
explanation.definitionFit: Being put to death for one's beliefs, as the philosopher was, is to suffer death as a martyr.

clue.text: Party Queen's executors

blocks.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, plus the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: The people who carry out the late Queen's will, at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: Executors suggests a will; read it plainly as people who execute, that is do, things.
explanation.definitionFit: Doers are people who carry things out, which is what executors literally do.

clue.text: Traitor in age of mistakes

indicators.note: in places the first item inside the second

explanation.surface: A treacherous person living in an era of blunders.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata is the Latin plural for errors, especially a list of printing corrections.

clue.text: Pierce in dress rehearsal

blocks.note: first meaning: stab right through with a blade
second meaning: a complete practice performance

explanation.surface: An actor named Pierce taking part in the final costume practice.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb form is two words and the noun hyphenated; the enumeration allows both. The stabbing sense suits Caesar's death.
explanation.definitionFit: To impale someone with a sword, and a full practice of a show, share the same phrase.

clue.text: Bog covering head of Robert Plant

indicators.note: covering means wrapped around, so the bog surrounds the letter
head of points to the first letter of the name

explanation.surface: Something in a marsh hides the face of the singer Robert Plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Plant, the Led Zeppelin singer, is a red herring: Plant is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A fern is a flowerless green plant that reproduces by spores.

clue.text: Fourteen head off touring in Transit

indicators.note: head off means the first letter is removed
touring means travelling around, so the remaining letters move about

explanation.surface: Fourteen people set off on tour in a Ford Transit van.
explanation.walkthrough: Fourteen looks like a cross-reference to 14-down, but here it is just the word; the capital on Transit disguises the plain phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A French phrase used in English for being on the way, travelling towards a destination.

clue.text: In retrospect, General Trebonius gutted to produce blade

indicators.note: in retrospect means looking back, so the letters are read from the end
gutted means the insides are removed, leaving only the outer letters

blocks.note: Robert E Lee, the Confederate general
first and last letters of the conspirator's name

explanation.surface: Looking back, a general's officer Trebonius was eviscerated with a sword.
explanation.walkthrough: Trebonius is another conspirator in Julius Caesar.
explanation.definitionFit: Steel is used as a literary metonym for a sword or blade made from that metal.

clue.text: A lot of mutinous old heads

indicators.note: mutinous means rebellious, so the letters refuse their order

explanation.surface: Many of the senior figures are in revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: Shedload is British slang for a large quantity, a great deal of something.

clue.text: Under no circumstances is Dad leaving cheese

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so the father's short name is taken away

blocks.note: pa is a familiar name for a father

explanation.surface: An insistence that father must never abandon the cheese board.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove PA from the front of PANEER to leave the poetic contraction NE'ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Ne'er is the poetic short form of never, meaning at no time at all.

clue.text: Soothsayer's craft needing no introduction

indicators.note: with no introduction the opening letter is left off

blocks.note: a coracle is a small round boat

explanation.surface: A fortune-teller's art is so famous it needs no introduction.
explanation.walkthrough: Craft looks like skill, but it is a boat; a soothsayer warned Caesar of the Ides of March.
explanation.definitionFit: An oracle is a person or shrine through whom prophecies are given, a foreteller of the future.

clue.text: Blue poet swaps love for anger

indicators.note: swaps means exchanges one thing for another, here the zero letter for a feeling

blocks.note: the Greek lyric poet of Lesbos
love is zero in tennis, the round letter

explanation.surface: A melancholy poet replaces love with fury.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue looks like sad, but it is the colour; love is tennis zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapphire is a deep, bright shade of blue named after the gemstone.

clue.text: Appeal to lawless plebeians leaving bin out

indicators.note: leaving something out means omitting it from the word
lawless means unruly, so the remaining letters fall out of order

explanation.surface: A plea to the riotous Roman commoners to stop leaving their rubbish out.
explanation.walkthrough: Take B, I and N from plebeians and rearrange what is left. The Roman mob riots in Julius Caesar.
explanation.definitionFit: Please is a polite request, an appeal or entreaty to someone.

clue.text: Casca's last in revolt to step up

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of the name
in places the letter inside the uprising

blocks.note: final letter of the conspirator's name

explanation.surface: The final conspirator Casca joins the rebellion and takes a step forward.
explanation.walkthrough: Casca struck the first blow at Caesar in Shakespeare's play.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise is to increase or intensify something, as when stepping up production.

clue.text: Cryptic clue with Brutus in alternative group

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A puzzle clue mentioning the assassin Brutus appears among a fringe crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A subculture is a set of people with beliefs or tastes at odds with the mainstream.

clue.text: Quote sense in speech

indicators.note: in speech means as heard spoken, not as spelt

blocks.note: sight is one of the five senses

explanation.surface: Repeat a sensible remark from someone's address.
explanation.definitionFit: To cite is to refer to or reproduce a passage or author as an authority.

clue.text: At heart, Caligula's terribly cross

indicators.note: at heart points to the central letters of the name
terribly means badly, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: the four central letters of the emperor's name

explanation.surface: Deep down, the emperor Caligula is furious.
explanation.walkthrough: Cross looks like angry, but it means a hybrid.
explanation.definitionFit: The ugli is a Jamaican citrus fruit, a hybrid of grapefruit and tangerine.

clue.text: Tribute beginning for Omar Little

indicators.note: beginning for points to the first letter of the name

explanation.surface: A memorial for Omar Little, the stick-up man from the TV series The Wire.
explanation.definitionFit: An obit, short for obituary, is a published notice honouring someone who has died.

clue.text: Old skill making a comeback for spear-carrier

indicators.note: making a comeback means returning, so the word runs backwards

explanation.surface: An ancient martial skill revived by a soldier carrying a spear.
explanation.walkthrough: A spear-carrier is the theatre term for a walk-on part, apt for a Roman crowd scene.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra is a performer with a small non-speaking role, like a soldier holding a spear on stage.

clue.text: Angela's broken dish

indicators.note: broken means smashed apart, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Angela has smashed a plate.
explanation.walkthrough: Dish looks like the plate that broke; it is the food.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasagne is an Italian baked dish of layered pasta sheets, sauce and cheese.
